assessment.summary: ERBB2 (HER2) is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged oncology targets in human medicine, with 14 approved drugs including monoclonal antibodies, small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. Structural data is exceptionally rich (63 PDB entries, best resolution 1.25Å, multiple ligand-bound structures), and chemical space is thoroughly explored with over 5,000 IC50 entries and a median potency of ~300 nM. Literature support is extensive and continuously growing, with active clinical and translational research across multiple cancer indications.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 74.0 with only 66.8% high-confidence residues suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular linkers or flexible loops) that may not be well-represented in crystal structures
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., HER2 mutations, bypass signalling) are not fully characterised for all approved agents, limiting next-generation drug design
Emerging indications (bladder cancer, colorectal cancer, liver fibrosis) have limited clinical validation compared to breast/gastric cancer
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP-binding pocket and extracellular domain epitopes remain incompletely mapped
Biomarker stratification (amplification vs. overexpression vs. mutation) for newer indications is still evolving
